en: The Philippine tarsier has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain, allowing it to see clearly in the dark.
National hero Jose Rizal was an ophthalmologist who used his medical skills to successfully treat his mother's cataracts.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park protects over a thousand marine species, including endangered hawksbill sea turtles and manta rays.
The tropical pitcher plant found on Mount Apo digests trapped insects to absorb essential nitrogen from poor soil.
The Aedes aegypti mosquito transmits the dengue virus to humans, making eliminating its breeding grounds crucial for public health.
The Philippine milkfish, or bangus, hatches in the ocean before migrating to coastal lagoons and freshwater lakes to mature.
The rare waling-waling orchid grows high up on tree branches in the rainforest to capture maximum sunlight.
The tamaraw, a dwarf buffalo endemic to Mindoro, has short V-shaped horns and prefers to live solitary lives.
Papaya fruits contain papain, a natural enzyme that helps the human stomach break down and digest dietary proteins.
The Philippine eagle possesses a shaggy head crest and uses its sharp talons to hunt flying foxes in forest canopies.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park features a massive cave system that serves as a roosting habitat for thousands of bats.
The Philippine mouse-deer, locally called pilandok, uses its small, pointed hooves to quietly navigate dense forest undergrowth.
